subject: Mutual Action Plan — Technical evaluation sprint assignments & targets
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Draft MAP: technical evaluation sprint (recap + asks)

Hi Sanjay,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on the evaluation goals. Per our discussion, I attached a one-page MAP draft focused on the technical evaluation sprint (HG_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf). Key things I pulled together here: milestone sequence, owners for each checkpoint, target close date, and explicit dependencies from your side.

Top-level proposal:
- Objective: run a 3-week technical evaluation that validates latency and cost at 95th/99th percentiles for our primary inference flows and confirms quality thresholds on your representative prompts.
- Target close date for the MAP: 2026-12-12 (3 weeks from kickoff).

Immediate asks for HealthGrid:
1) Confirm the model shortlist (we suggested: Llama-3-13B-8k, Mistral-7B-v1, Redstone-13B-8k-quant). If you want a different candidate, let us know by EOD Friday.
2) Share a canonical prompt set (<=200 prompts) and 3 representative production traffic traces (anonymized).
3) Provide access to a staging K8s namespace or a temporary S3 bucket for logs by Monday 11/23.

Proposed milestone owners (internal):
- Benchmark orchestration & test harness: Ben Carter
- Latency/cost profiling & SLOs: Lauren Bishop
- Overall coordination + results readout: me (Alex) / Marissa as backup

Attached: HG_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf, LLM_benchmark_template.xlsx (template for the prompt set), latency-cost-targets.csv (our suggested targets).

Can you confirm the shortlist and if the 12/12 target is feasible? If yes, will propose a kickoff for next Tuesday (11/24) at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft MAP: technical evaluation sprint (recap + asks)

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and the draft. We're generally aligned and like the proposed three-week cadence. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Shortlist: Accept Llama-3-13B-8k and Mistral-7B-v1. We want to swap Redstone-13B-8k-quant for a smaller quantized candidate (e.g., Redstone-7B-quant) to see tradeoffs on cost. Can you include that variant?
- Prompt set: we'll export a 150-prompt subset and drop it in the S3 location you provide by Monday (11/23).
- Staging access: we can open an IAM role for a temporary S3 bucket and a read-only view of a staging namespace in our AWS account — will need your security contact to accept the invite.

On targets: the 95th/99th latency targets look aggressive but useful. We may need to scope the first run to 8k context rather than full 32k to speed iteration. Our goal is to validate cost/latency regimes first.

I'll be on the kickoff next Tue if scheduled.

— Sanjay
Chief Product Officer
HealthGrid
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@healthgrid.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: technical evaluation sprint (recap + asks)

Alex / team — tagging in with a proposed test plan change and tooling notes. Quoting relevant bits from Alex's draft below for context.

> Objective: run a 3-week technical evaluation that validates latency and cost at 95th/99th percentiles for our primary inference flows and confirms quality thresholds on your representative prompts.

Given HealthGrid's ask to keep iteration fast, here's my recommended adjustments:
1) Kickoff (day 0): confirm prompt set and upload. Baseline runs on 8k context with 200-500 warmup tokens.
2) Week 1: single-instance latency profile across the three model candidates + quantized 7B variant. Produce p50/p95/p99 for token generation (both cold and warm cache).
3) Week 2: cost-per-1000-token simulation under our traffic mix (batched and unbatched), plus memory/kv-cache behavior checks.
4) Week 3: quality check (prompt pass/fail on acceptance criteria) and a short readout to stakeholders.

Benchmarks & success criteria (concrete):
- Latency: p95 <= 450ms token-gen for 8k average sequences, p99 <= 950ms (cold) for targeted flows.
- Cost: target < $0.015 per 1k tokens on average with batching; we will report both raw compute and effective per-call cost.
- Quality: >= 90% pass rate on the canonical prompt set acceptance rubric (we'll share rubric columns in LLM_benchmark_template.xlsx).

Tooling: I'll own the benchmark harness (we'll use the attached template). Need HealthGrid to provide anonymized traces and the prompt set. For the S3 access and IAM role, point security to lauren_bishop@redwood.com.

Ben
Benchmarking Lead
Redwood Inference

Sanjay / Alex — security/ops notes on onboarding and timeline.

- I'll send an invite for cross-account IAM role access today. Please confirm the external email for the IAM trust (we'll send the role arn to the sanjay.patel@healthgrid.com address unless you'd prefer a different contact).
- For the S3 bucket, we'll provide a write-only presigned path for the prompt set and traces by EOD 11/23. Expect bucket path and short instructions in a separate email.
- Dependency: if HealthGrid needs a VPC peering or a private endpoint instead of S3, that will add ~2 business days to the timeline. Call out if that's the case.

On the 8k vs 32k context: agree to start with 8k for the sprint; we can expand after the initial readout if results justify.

Lauren Bishop

Redwood Inference

Sanjay — thanks for the quick turnaround and the go-ahead on the shortlist (we swapped in Redstone-7B-quant per your note). Summary and next steps below — please confirm and we'll lock the kickoff for Tue 11/24 at 10am PT: 

Agreed checklist before kickoff:

- HealthGrid to accept IAM cross-account role for read-only staging access — security contact: lauren_bishop@redwood.com.
- Models to test: Llama-3-13B-8k, Mistral-7B-v1, Redstone-7B-quant.
- Targets: p95 latency <= 450ms (8k), p99 <= 950ms (cold), cost target < $0.015/1k tokens.
- Owners: Ben (benchmarks/harness), Lauren (security/onboarding), Alex/Marissa (coordination & readout).

Deliverables & dates:
- 11/24: Kickoff + test plan finalized (meeting minutes uploaded to Drive).
- 11/26: Baseline latency profile (Week 1 deliverable).
- 12/03: Cost simulation & memory/kv checks (Week 2 deliverable).
- 12/10: Quality acceptance runs + stakeholder readout.
- 12/12: MAP close (decision point: proceed to pilot on Dedicated or iterate).

If that aligns, I'll send the calendar invite for 11/24 10am PT and a short agenda. Thanks all for the quick responses — excited to get this rolling.

Best,
